legend: You are given a set S$$$S$$$ of n$$$n$$$ distinct integers. You will also receive q$$$q$$$ queries, each of one of the following two types:
Query Type 1 (1x)$$$(1\; x)$$$:   If x$$$x$$$ is currently in the set S$$$S$$$, remove it.
Otherwise, add x$$$x$$$ to the set.
Query Type 2 (2t)$$$(2\; t)$$$:   Print the cumulative bitwise XOR of (x+t)$$$(x + t)$$$ over all x∈S$$$x \in S$$$. Formally, print ⨁x∈S(x+t)$$$\displaystyle\bigoplus_{x \in S} (x + t)$$$.
input: The first line of the input contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and q$$$q$$$ (1≤n,q≤3⋅105$$$1 \leq n,q \leq 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the initial size of the set and the number of queries, respectively.
The next line of the input will contain n$$$n$$$ distinct integers x1,x2⋯xn$$$x_1, x_2 \cdots x_n$$$ (0≤xi<220$$$0 \le x_i  \lt  2^{20}$$$)  — the initial set.

The next q$$$q$$$ lines of the input will describe the queries. Each of them will contain a query of the form 1x$$$1\; x$$$ or 2t$$$2\; t$$$ (0≤x,t<220$$$0 \le x, t  \lt  2^{20}$$$), representing the query in the format described above.
It is guaranteed that there is at least one query of type 2$$$2$$$.
output: For each query of type 2$$$2$$$, print the cumulative bitwise XOR of (x+t)$$$(x+t)$$$ over all x∈S$$$x \in S$$$.
note: In the sample case, at the time of the first type 2$$$2$$$ query, we have S={1,6,15}$$$S = \{1, 6, 15\}$$$. Since t=0$$$t = 0$$$ for this query, we print the value (1+0)⊕(6+0)⊕(15+0)=1⊕6⊕15=8$$(1 + 0) \oplus (6 + 0) \oplus (15 + 0) = 1 \oplus 6 \oplus 15 = 8$$ At the time of the second type 2$$$2$$$ query, we have S={1,5,10,15}$$$S = \{1, 5, 10, 15\}$$$. Since t=3$$$t = 3$$$ for this query, we print the value (1+3)⊕(5+3)⊕(10+3)⊕(15+3)=4⊕8⊕13⊕18=19$$(1 + 3) \oplus (5 + 3) \oplus (10 + 3) \oplus (15 + 3) = 4 \oplus 8 \oplus 13 \oplus 18 = 19$$
